New analysis: between country explanation for rates

We know that changes over time in both a) how retractions are reported, and b) retraction watch’s data processing practice for them make temporal patterns complex to interpret. What is more robust is inter-country comparisons.

Applying reasons: United Kingdom vs Other OECD

Statistical comparison of the retraction reasons between the UK and the rest of the OECD excluding the mass retractions. The for each period (pre and post 2017) and retraction reason, computes the proportion and count of retractions in the UK and the rest of the OECD, the difference in proportions, a two-sample proportion test p-value and its Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.

AI retractions by country and scenario

How these plots are built:

  • The full data is used, so each scenario’s name says whether mass retractions are included.
  • Retractions and SCImago publication counts both cover papers published in 2017–2025, when almost all AI retractions happen.
  • Countries with no AI retractions are shown at 0, on a pseudo-log axis (linear near 0, logarithmic above).
  • Bars are exact 95% confidence intervals: Poisson for rates, binomial for shares.
  • Rates per paper are only shown for the “All” scenarios. SCImago counts all of a country’s papers, not only its domestic ones, so a domestic rate would divide domestic retractions by all papers. For domestic scenarios use the share of retractions that mention AI (next plots), where both counts are domestic.
